resources.string: Use a photo you took yourself and haven\'t posted anywhere. Someone holding the original can compare the two.
Stays a JPEG with the camera\'s own compression, so it looks like any other photo from your phone.
Saved as a PNG. A camera photo saved as PNG is unusual in itself, so JPEG is usually the better choice.
Room for up to %1$d bytes of text. Detectability stays low up to about %2$d.
Room for up to %1$d bytes of text. Anything hidden in an image this size is easier to detect.
Paste their age1… key. Only their secret key will open it.
A second message under a second passphrase. If someone makes you open the image, give them this one. Nobody can tell whether an image has a decoy.
Off removes location, time and device details. Turn on only if the photo needs them to look normal.
Hiding. This can take several seconds on a large photo.
Write a message or choose a file.
The decoy needs a different passphrase.
Send it as a file or document. A messenger\'s photo mode recompresses the picture and destroys what\'s hidden. Don\'t share the original photo anywhere.
The photo couldn\'t be taken. Try again.
The camera wasn\'t allowed. Pick a photo you took earlier instead.
Photo taken just now. It isn\'t saved anywhere else.
You\'ve hidden something in this photo before. Anyone holding two versions of one photo can compare them, so use a new one.
This photo has no camera details, so it may be a download or a saved messenger image. If a copy exists elsewhere, it can be compared with yours. A photo you just took is safer.
This came from Downloads, so a copy may exist online and could be compared with yours. A photo you just took is safer.
Choose the image, or share it to StegPony from another app.
Enter the passphrase, or paste a secret key (AGE-SECRET-KEY-1…). To skip this next time, add your key on the Keys screen.

plurals.item: Leave this empty to open it with your key. Enter a passphrase only for an image hidden with one, or paste a different secret key.
Leave this empty to open it with your %1$d keys. Enter a passphrase only for an image hidden with one, or paste a different secret key.

resources.string: Either nothing is hidden in this image, or it was hidden with a different passphrase. StegPony can\'t tell which, and neither can anyone else.
No keys yet. Create one to receive images hidden for you, then share its public key.
A new key works with age, so the public key can also receive files from age and AgePony.
Key created. Share its public key with whoever will hide things for you.
Import an age identity file, or an OpenPGP secret key with a Curve25519 encryption key (cv25519 or X25519).
This OpenPGP key is protected. Its passphrase is used once to unlock it and is not kept.
Add the public keys of people you hide things for.
You already have this key, as %1$s.
Anything hidden for this key can no longer be opened on this phone. There is no undo.
You can add them again from their public key.
The saved keys can\'t be opened, so they are lost either way. Starting over deletes them and anything hidden for them can no longer be opened on this phone. There is no undo.
This age identity file is protected with a passphrase. Export it without one, import it, then delete the copy.
Your keys couldn\'t be opened (%1$s). Nothing has been changed.
Scan this with StegPony or AgePony to add it as a contact.
Point the camera at a QR code with an age1… key, or an OpenPGP key from PGPony.
Part %1$d of %2$d. Scan the next code.
That QR code isn\'t a public key StegPony can use.
That\'s a secret key. Scan the public key instead, and keep the secret one private.
The camera wasn\'t allowed, so the QR code can\'t be scanned. Paste the key or load it from a file instead.
What was shared isn\'t a public key StegPony can use. It needs an age1… key or a Curve25519 OpenPGP key.
Added %1$s. Share its public key like any other.
Hardware key (the secret stays on the key)
Only the public key saved here is removed. The hardware key itself is not touched, and you can add it again.
The key\'s user PIN. It goes to the key once and is not kept.
Hold your key to the back of the phone and keep it there until this finishes.
Hold your key to the back of the phone, or plug it in. Keep it there until this finishes.
Working with the plugged-in key. If it blinks, touch it.
Allow StegPony to use the plugged-in key when Android asks.
NFC is off. Turn it on in Android settings, or plug the key in.
This phone has no NFC. Plug the key in.
This phone can\'t reach a hardware key: no NFC and no USB host support.
Done. You can take the key away.

This key has no decryption key yet. Generate or move a cv25519 key onto it first.

Ask for your fingerprint, face or screen lock to open StegPony, and again after a minute away or when the screen turns off.
Set a screen lock on the phone first. The app lock uses it.
Also keeps Hide out of the recent-apps view. Reveal and Keys always block screenshots.

Changes the name and icon in the launcher and in share menus. It doesn\'t hide the app: the real name still shows in Android\'s app settings and in F-Droid. Some launchers remove the home-screen shortcut when this changes; add it again from the app drawer.
Warn when a cover is reused
StegPony keeps fingerprints of the photos you\'ve hidden in, encrypted and on this phone only, to warn before one is used again. Turning this off forgets them.

Hiding lowers the odds of being noticed. It doesn\'t make it impossible. A large message in a small photo, a cover that exists somewhere else, or someone who already knows you use StegPony all weaken it. Anything that re-encodes the image, such as resizing, filters or a messenger\'s photo mode, destroys what\'s hidden.
This kind of image can\'t be used. StegPony works with JPEG and PNG.
